BASELINE CIRCULATING T CELL BIOMARKERS FOR 1-YEAR OVERALL SURVIVAL IN NIVOLUMAB + CHEMO PATIENTS (PICI0002 TRIAL, ARM A1)
=========================================================================================================================

COHORT
- Arm A1 (gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel + nivolumab): 34 patients total
- With baseline CyTOF data: 25 patients (14 OS events, 11 censored)
- OS range: 43-779 days, median 445 days

ANALYSIS
- Seven T cell populations measured by CyTOF at C1D1 (baseline, pre-treatment)
- Median-split Kaplan-Meier with log-rank tests + BH-FDR correction (7 tests)
- Cox proportional hazards regression on continuous frequencies (per-1-SD hazard ratios)
- Proportional hazards assumption verified for all populations

SIGNIFICANT FINDINGS (4 populations with log-rank p < 0.05, all surviving BH-FDR):

1. NKT CELLS (% of leukocytes) — PROTECTIVE BIOMARKER
   Log-rank p = 0.005 (FDR = 0.025)
   High (>1.64%): 1-year OS = 90.0%, Low: 36.4%
   Per-SD HR = 0.389 (95% CI: 0.166-0.908), Cox p = 0.029
   Interpretation: Higher baseline NKT cell frequency is associated with substantially improved survival. NKT cells bridge innate and adaptive immunity; their presence may indicate an immunologically primed state responsive to anti-PD-1 therapy.

2. Tbet+ TCRgd+ T CELLS (% of TCRgd T cells) — PROTECTIVE BIOMARKER
   Log-rank p = 0.025 (FDR = 0.044)
   High (>79.2%): 1-year OS = 80.8%, Low: 45.5%
   Per-SD HR = 0.301 (95% CI: 0.150-0.603), Cox p = 0.0007 (FDR = 0.005)
   Interpretation: The strongest result in Cox regression. Gamma-delta T cells expressing T-bet have potent cytotoxic and cytokine-producing capacity, suggesting innate-like cytotoxic immunity may be critical for anti-PD-1 response.

3. Tbet+ T CELLS (% of CD3+ cells) — PROTECTIVE BIOMARKER
   Log-rank p = 0.011 (FDR = 0.025)
   High (>17.9%): 1-year OS = 80.8%, Low: 45.5%
   Per-SD HR = 0.525 (95% CI: 0.252-1.094), Cox p = 0.085
   Interpretation: T-bet is the master Th1 transcription factor. Higher Th1-polarized T cell frequencies at baseline predict better response to anti-PD-1 + chemo, consistent with the requirement for interferon-gamma-producing immunity.

4. Ki-67+ T CELLS (% of CD3+ cells) — ADVERSE BIOMARKER
   Log-rank p = 0.010 (FDR = 0.025)
   High (>96.6%): 1-year OS = 33.3%, Low: 100%
   Per-SD HR = 2.276 (95% CI: 1.040-4.979), Cox p = 0.040
   Interpretation: High baseline T cell proliferation (Ki-67) paradoxically predicts worse survival. Note: values were compressed (83-100%), and this may reflect chronic immune activation without effective tumor control, rather than productive anti-tumor immunity.

NON-SIGNIFICANT POPULATIONS (log-rank p > 0.05):
- HLA-DR+ T cells (p = 0.36)
- HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD4 T Cells (p = 0.79)
- HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T Cells (p = 0.96)

LIMITATIONS
- Small sample (n=25, 14 events) limits power and generalizability
- 9 of 34 Arm A1 patients lacked baseline CyTOF data (potential selection bias)
- No multivariate adjustment (too few events per covariate)
- Single timepoint analysis; on-treatment dynamics not assessed
- Compressed Ki-67 distribution makes clinical interpretation of "high vs low" questionable

CONCLUSION
Three baseline circulating T cell populations are protective biomarkers for 1-year overall survival in patients receiving nivolumab + chemotherapy: NKT cells (strongest KM signal), Tbet+ TCRgd+ gamma-delta T cells (strongest Cox signal), and Tbet+ T cells. One population — Ki-67+ T cells — is an adverse biomarker. These findings suggest that a Th1-polarized, innate-like cytotoxic T cell profile at baseline predicts favorable response to anti-PD-1-based immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer. However, these results require validation in larger cohorts.
